code: library(tabpfn) set.seed(364) reg_mod <- tab_pfn(mtcars[1:25, -1], mtcars$mpg[1:25]) reg_mod #> TabPFN Regression Model #> Training set #> ℹ 25 data points #> ℹ 10 predictors predict(reg_mod, mtcars[26:32, -1]) #> # A tibble: 7 × 1 #>   .pred #>   <dbl> #> 1  31.4 #> 2  24.3 #> 3  24.8 #> 4  16.4 #> 5  18.9 #> 6  14.4 #> 7  22.5 library(modeldata) #>  #> Attaching package: 'modeldata' #> The following object is masked from 'package:datasets': #>  #>     penguins library(ggplot2)  two_cls_train <- parabolic[1:400,  ] two_cls_val   <- parabolic[401:500,] grid <- expand.grid(X1 = seq(-5.1, 5.0, length.out = 25),                      X2 = seq(-5.5, 4.0, length.out = 25))  set.seed(3824) cls_mod <- tab_pfn(class ~ ., data = two_cls_train)  grid_pred <- predict(cls_mod, grid) grid_pred #> # A tibble: 625 × 3 #>    .pred_Class1 .pred_Class2 .pred_class #>           <dbl>        <dbl> <fct>       #>  1        0.997      0.00270 Class1      #>  2        0.998      0.00228 Class1      #>  3        0.998      0.00183 Class1      #>  4        0.998      0.00177 Class1      #>  5        0.998      0.00176 Class1      #>  6        0.998      0.00243 Class1      #>  7        0.995      0.00479 Class1      #>  8        0.987      0.0126  Class1      #>  9        0.950      0.0501  Class1      #> 10        0.754      0.246   Class1      #> # ℹ 615 more rows cbind(grid, grid_pred) |>   ggplot(aes(X1, X2)) +   geom_point(     data = two_cls_val,     aes(col = class, pch = class),     alpha = 3 / 4,     cex = 3   ) +   geom_contour(     aes(z = .pred_Class1),     breaks = 1 / 2,     col = "black",     linewidth = 1   ) +   coord_equal(ratio = 1)

title: Eagerly initialize the TabPFN Python library — tabpfn_initialize
text: Forces Python tabpfn library (PyTorch dependency) load now instead first use. PyTorch bundles OpenMP runtime, loading package uses OpenMP avoids segmentation fault described https://github.com/tidymodels/tabpfn/issues/34. work, call first thing session, using tabpfn::tabpfn_initialize() (:: prefix runs library(tabpfn) package might load OpenMP, recipes):
code: tabpfn::tabpfn_initialize() library(tabpfn) suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(recipes)) fit_obj <- tab_pfn(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)

title: tabpfn (development version)
text: New tabpfn_initialize() eagerly loads Python tabpfn library (PyTorch). Call right library(tabpfn) OpenMP-using packages avoid segmentation fault described #34. "r-tabpfn" environment (created install_tabpfn()) Python installation reticulate resolves , tabpfn Python library now imported eagerly load time PyTorch claims OpenMP packages can, avoiding segmentation fault (#34). New install_tabpfn() sets persistent "r-tabpfn" Python virtual environment. version argument pin specific tabpfn release , default, offers upgrade existing environment newer release available. Added type argument consistent parsnip. Defaults NULL, produce prediction types.
